description.narrative: The development objective of Revenue Administration Reform Project is to improve the effectiveness of operational functions of Montenegro's Tax Administration (MTA) and to reduce the compliance costs for corporate taxpayers. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Institutional Development, aims to help enhance the strategic focus of management, increase attention to integrity, strengthen staff management and training, develop the analytical capacity required to support strategic management within MTA, improve the legal framework and the appeals function, and institute a modern revenue administration. Subcomponent one will focus on institutional and organizational development, enhancing strategic focus and planning capacity; strengthening executive, managerial, technical and operational capacity; and includes the introduction of an enhanced monitoring system to assist in the management of the MTA's performance. Subcomponent two will focus on strengthening the capacity for managing the change process. Subcomponent three will strengthen the MTA's capacity to coordinate project implementation and contract management. 2) The second component, Business Processes, supports modernization of MTA's business processes and improvements in operational effectiveness. This component has three sub-components. Subcomponent one will: introduce international best practices into the operational functions of the MTA; strengthen registration and return processing; formalize risk analysis in audit selection and enforcement activities, improve business analytics to identify where limited MTA resources should be deployed to return the best results or meet specific MTA objectives; and strengthen anti-fraud and criminal investigation capacity of the MTA. Subcomponent two will cleanse and rationalize data from the existing system in the first years of the project and enhance the IT infrastructure, including the enterprise architecture, data center, security, and disaster recovery plans. Subcomponent three will develop the specifications for the new IRMS system; procure, localize and implement a commercial Integrated Revenue Management System to replace the current system; and procure the necessary equipment required to implement the IRMS system. 3) The third component, Taxpayer Services, aims to finance activities to modernize taxpayer services and increase understanding of revenue laws, procedures, rights and obligations of taxpayers, and thereby reduce the compliance burden to taxpayers, and strengthen external and internal communications.

The development objective of the project is to improve the effectiveness of operational functions of Montenegro's tax administration and to reduce the compliance costs for corporate taxpayers. The project supports Montenegro's long-term vision of a revenue administration that operates with streamlined risk-based business processes that contribute to the efficient collection of taxes and social contributions from all sources of economic activity. Increased compliance will generate a more robust revenue stream to provide essential services to citizens. Improvements in revenue administration capacity will also support the country's goal for EU accession and economic integration with EU member states.

title.narrative: Estimated tax gap is calculated annually and trend analysis published annually by year 5

actual.value: MTA has not conducted a tax gap analysis and is working on a methodology with the consultant hired under the project.

baseline.value: No methodology for Tax Gap for VAT estimation

target.value: 6% reduction in Tax Gap for VAT compared to 2020 value

actual.value: End target is achieved based on the available data from 2022. The VAT Gap methodology is adopted and regularly updated by the MTA.

title.narrative: Payment compliance rate for CIT and VAT
Percentage of tax returns filed on time
Achieved processing of almost 90% of VAT refund claims within 30 days for predominantly exporters and 60 days for the rest of the taxpayers according to domestic law
Real-time information for VAT transactions available to MRCA

baseline.value: no real time EFI system in place

target.value: EFI system available 99.5% of the time for all transactions

title.narrative: Tax Administration's staff satisfaction with the new skills and ability to apply them, disaggregated by gender

baseline.value: 68 index of tax administration staff respondents indicate satisfaction (men 71 index, women 66 index) - baseline set in 2019

target.value: 78 - no gap between male and female

actual.value: Conducted (2022). Index of tax administration staff satisfaction: 60. (men: 56, women: 62) - no change from previous - next survey data will be available in April 2025.

title.narrative: Taxpayers satisfaction with tax administration's quality of taxpayers services and integrity of tax administration staff

actual.value: 76 down from 82 in 2019 - no change from previous - next survey data will be available in April 2025.

title.narrative: Taxpayer satisfaction with Simplicity of Calculation of VAT and submission of tax returns to Revenue and Customs Administration

actual.value: Index of 58 for satisfied and there has been no change since the last reporting period.

title.narrative: Development and implementation of the DWH/BI

target.value: Risk-based analysis applied by MRCA at the HQ and regional level using DWH/BI (2025)

actual.value: DWH/BI contract is expired and the MTA initiated contract closure. Only the Data Analytics using EFI data has been delivered and now being used by MTA. partial achievement of the indicator.

title.narrative: Use of EFI in VAT collection and refund processes

baseline.value: EFI transaction data not utilized for validating VAT payments and refunds

target.value: EFI transaction data used by MRCA sector for tax inspection and large taxpayers for processes of VAT refunds

actual.value: The indicator has been met. The EFI transaction data used by MTA sector for tax inspection and large taxpayers for processes of VAT refunds

title.narrative: Use of EFI in deployment of inspection

baseline.value: EFI used as reference in inspection/audit by the inspection and large taxpayer departments in HQ (2022)

target.value: EFI used in deployment of real-time inspections and audit in HQ and regional offices and audit module fully operational

actual.value: In Sector for inspection control â€“ Group for risk analysis, selection of cases for control and reporting, analysis of claims for VAT refunds are based on analysis of data from EFI (analysis of received /sent invoices for each taxpayer individually). Also, for planning purposes of non-regular controls, data used are received from Department for EFI (number of cancelled invoices, data on termination of EFI registration, data for taxpayers which are not recording regularly transactions). Regional tax inspectors during execution of full and partial controls are using data from EFI, based on which irregularities are recorded, as well as need for additional/side controls.

target.value: all 4 core modules (registration, tax accounting, taxpayer services, inspection) and other special modules are fully operational

actual.value: IRMS contract under implementation with delays and catching up. The conceptual design, system architecture, and data migration plan have been adopted by the MTA and payments against this deliverable have been made.
